How long is the stay for otoplasty and suture check-ups?

Plan a minimum of 5 to 7 nights in Istanbul for standalone adult otoplasty, or 7 to 10 nights if combining ear pinning with chin or jawline contouring. This window covers pre-operative blood work, surgery, the first dressing change at 48 to 72 hours, and a final suture inspection before your surgeon signs fit-to-fly clearance.

Booking a 3-night sprint creates avoidable stress. The [NHS ear correction surgery guide](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/ear-correction-surgery/) notes that head bandages must stay clean and dry until removal, and patients cannot wash their hair until dressings come off. Leaving Istanbul before that first check means flying in a bulky turban wrap without a local clinician confirming there is no hematoma or pressure sore behind the ear.

body.text: What headband protection is needed on the flight home?

Once your surgeon removes the bulky post-operative bandage, you will typically switch to a wide, breathable, non-compressive elastic headband that covers the ears completely without folding the cartilage. The [American Society of Plastic Surgeons recovery guide](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/cosmetic-procedures/ear-surgery/recovery) stresses protecting healing ears from accidental bumps, overhead-bin knocks, and side-sleeping pressure during early recovery.

On the aircraft, cabin dry air and fatigue make it easy to lean against a window wall or knock an ear against a seat headrest. Pack a U-shaped memory-foam neck pillow to keep your head centered, wear a button-up or zip-front top so nothing pulls over your ears, and bring a spare clean headband in your carry-on bag. Avoid over-ear headphones and tight sunglasses for the first several weeks unless your surgeon explicitly approves them.
How do local anesthesia vs general anesthesia options compare?

Adult standalone otoplasty is frequently performed under local anesthesia with or without light sedation, whereas children and patients combining otoplasty with facial contouring usually receive general anesthesia. As [Cleveland Clinic's ear pinning overview](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/24664-ear-pinning) explains, anesthesia choice depends on age, procedural scope, and medical history—and directly affects hospital discharge timing and hotel transport needs.

body.text: What realistic 2026 costs apply at vetted hospitals?

In 2026, realistic bilateral otoplasty pricing at accredited private hospitals in Istanbul typically ranges from €1,800 to €3,500 for standalone ear pinning, rising to €4,500–€7,500 when combined with chin augmentation or buccal fat contouring. Quotes below €1,400 often omit hospital facility fees, anesthesiologist charges, or post-operative medications—so always request an itemized written breakdown before booking flights.

Before paying any deposit, verify that the hospital holds an active International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate via the [Turkish Ministry of Health Health Tourism Department](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html), governed by the [Regulation on International Health Tourism and Tourist Health](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-108974/regulation-on-international-health-tourism-and-tourist-health.html). faq.q: Can I fly home 2 days after otoplasty in Istanbul?
faq.a: Flying 48 hours after surgery is generally discouraged because your primary head dressing is still in place and early swelling peaks within 72 hours. Staying 5 to 7 nights allows your surgeon to remove the wrap, inspect sutures, and issue written fit-to-fly clearance.

faq.q: Will I need stitch removal in Türkiye or at home?
faq.a: Many surgeons use dissolvable sutures behind the ear, while others place non-absorbable stitches removed at days 7 to 10. Ask your surgical team in writing during your pre-trip consultation so your stay length matches your suture plan.

faq.q: Does cabin pressure damage healing ear cartilage?
faq.a: Cabin pressure changes affect the middle ear rather than external ear cartilage, so pressure alone rarely harms an otoplasty repair. The bigger flight risks are swelling, accidental trauma from headrests or bags, and inadequate pain control.

faq.q: Can I wear glasses after ear pinning surgery?
faq.a: Glasses resting behind the ear can press directly on fresh incisions and cartilage sutures. Ask your surgeon whether you should switch to contact lenses or tape glasses frames to your forehead during the first two weeks.
